clue.text: Players shifted gate behind the scenes

indicators.note: things shifted have been moved about, so the letters of the next word change places

blocks.note: backs are players in defensive positions in rugby or football
the letters of gate rearranged

explanation.surface: Stagehands moved a gate around while out of the audience's sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Players' looks like actors, fitting the theatre picture, but here it is sporting backs.
explanation.definitionFit: Backstage is the adverb for the area of a theatre hidden from the audience, hence out of public view.

indicators.note: something hiding in a place is tucked inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a garden bed is a plot of ground
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Something became settled while concealed in a scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' suggests a scheme, fitting 'hiding', but it is a patch of garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Based means founded or set up somewhere, a synonym of established in the sense of located.

clue.text: Polite company, undergraduate primarily, so true to form

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so only the opening letter of the preceding word counts
letters put into form are shaped anew, so the words before are rearranged

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for company
first letter of undergraduate
the letters of so true rearranged

explanation.surface: A well-mannered firm, with a student in the lead, behaves true to type.
explanation.definitionFit: Courteous is a direct synonym of polite: showing good manners and consideration.

indicators.note: material put up for development is reworked, so the letters before are rebuilt into something new

blocks.note: the ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A vendor makes use of a report to plan expansion.
explanation.definitionFit: A superstore is a very large shop, and a shop is something that sells goods to customers.

clue.text: Sign is up, scribbled in card

indicators.note: a scribble is messy writing, so the letters of the words before get jumbled
in places the jumbled letters inside the word that follows

blocks.note: an ace is a playing card
the letters of is up rearranged

explanation.surface: An omen is posted, jotted down on a card.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled letters sit inside ACE: A-USPI-CE.
explanation.definitionFit: An auspice is an omen or portent, originally a sign read from the flight of birds.

blocks.note: first meaning: fast and non-stop, as of a train or delivery
second meaning: to put into words

explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like it introduces an example, but it is a verb in its own right.
explanation.definitionFit: Express is an adjective for a direct, non-stop service and a verb for stating a thought or feeling.

blocks.note: first meaning: stiffly correct in manner
second meaning: slang for a corpse

explanation.walkthrough: 'Formal body' reads like an official committee; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes rigid, unrelaxed behaviour and is also slang for a dead person.

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting raises the bottom to the top, so the word is read upwards

blocks.note: shirts are examples of tops; 'say' marks the example

explanation.surface: Notice that some shirts have been stolen.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to see or notice it, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Cover up a little secret: Nicaraguan uprising

indicators.note: a little of the following words means only part of them, a run of consecutive letters
in a down clue, rising means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the end of secret and the start of Nicaraguan

explanation.surface: Hushing up a minor secret about a revolt in Nicaragua.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nicaraguan uprising' suggests a revolution, but uprising just turns the hidden letters around.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to bury, which literally covers a body up with earth.

clue.text: How tango is choreographed: Romeo taking hand, first of all, in Texas city

indicators.note: first of all asks for the opening letter of each of the words just before

blocks.note: the tango is a dance for two people
Romeo is R in the NATO alphabet
the opening letters of taking and hand

explanation.surface: A dance instruction scene: Romeo leads his partner by the hand in a Texan city.
explanation.walkthrough: The first block is a cryptic phrase: a tango is choreographed 'for two'. Then R and the initials T, H follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Fort Worth is a large city in north Texas, next to Dallas.

blocks.note: first meaning: to baffle
second meaning: what is left after a tree or limb is cut off

explanation.walkthrough: 'Puzzle piece' reads as a jigsaw part; split it after the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for baffling someone and a noun for the short remnant left after cutting.

blocks.note: to sup is to drink in sips
porter is a dark beer, close kin to stout

explanation.surface: Someone recommends a pint of dark beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stout' looks like an adjective (fat, brave) but it is the beer.
explanation.definitionFit: An advocate is a backer of a cause, which is exactly what a supporter is.

blocks.note: first meaning: ascertained or established, past tense
second meaning: firm in purpose

explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like someone labelled as resolute; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the past tense of finding something out and an adjective for being firmly set on a goal.

indicators.note: having no tail means the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: the crown is the top of the head

explanation.surface: A description of a bird that has a head but lacks a tail.
explanation.definitionFit: The crow is a large black bird of the corvid family.

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for a Democrat in US politics
someone voters might choose for a post

explanation.surface: An attractive Democratic candidate looks a winner.
explanation.definitionFit: Delectable means delightful or very attractive, so it fits charming as an adjective.

blocks.note: scot was an old tax or levy, as in scot-free
to tie up, as an animal

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned chore: put the burden down and tie up the dog.
explanation.walkthrough: Scot is an archaic word for a tax, surviving in scot-free.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottie is a Scottish terrier, a small wiry-coated breed.

clue.text: Problem reported on newspaper, not in every case

indicators.note: reported means passed on by word of mouth, so we want a word that sounds like the clue word

blocks.note: a sum is a maths problem; it sounds like some
The Times, the London daily

explanation.surface: A problem was covered in the press, but it does not happen every time.
explanation.definitionFit: Sometimes means occasionally, on some occasions but not always.

clue.text: Something found in the kitchen, large vessel

blocks.note: first meaning: a pan for cooking food by steam
second meaning: a steamship

explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a pot to go with the kitchen, but it is a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a cooking utensil that uses steam and a ship driven by a steam engine.

blocks.note: first meaning: without equal
second meaning: lacking a fixture, with no game arranged

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the jokey second reading, taking the word literally as 'without a match'.
explanation.definitionFit: Matchless means peerless, unrivalled; read literally, a side without a match has no game to play.

clue.text: One removed from invalid procedure — some blow?

indicators.note: removed from tells us to take something out of the following word

blocks.note: Roman numeral one
a trial voided because of an error

explanation.surface: Someone dismissed after a botched trial: quite a blow?
explanation.walkthrough: 'some blow' hints at a setback, but it means something that blows hard.
explanation.definitionFit: The mistral is a strong cold wind blowing down the Rhône valley into southern France.

blocks.note: L abbreviates length
taken as written
the yard is an imperial unit of length

explanation.surface: A rope measured out in old imperial units.
explanation.definitionFit: A lanyard is a cord or short rope, used on ships or worn around the neck.

indicators.note: did you say asks us to hear the word rather than read it

blocks.note: an adulterer cheats on a spouse

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a love rat is a predator.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheetah is a big cat that hunts antelope, a classic predator.

clue.text: Line taken on nincompoop overseen by Conservative body

blocks.note: C abbreviates Conservative
an arc is a curved line
a fool

explanation.surface: A political tale: a fool supervised by a Tory takes on the party line.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'overseen by' means the Conservative letter sits on top of what follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A carcass is a dead body, usually of an animal.

clue.text: Old garment, article secured from the back

indicators.note: reading from the back means starting at the end and working forwards

blocks.note: the indefinite article
got means obtained

explanation.surface: An item of ancient clothing fastened at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: The toga was the loose outer garment worn by citizens of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Yellow and white food served up, filled with gold stuff

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means presented bottom to top
something filled with another thing holds it inside

blocks.note: an egg has a yellow yolk and white albumen
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: An egg dish brought to the table with golden stuffing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuff' looks like a noun ending the picture, but it is the verb: to stuff oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: To gorge is to eat greedily, which is what stuffing yourself means.

clue.text: Needing support once hurt, sick oddly given treatment

indicators.note: oddly keeps only the odd-numbered letters of the word before
treated material is processed and reworked, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to rearrange
the first and third letters of sick

explanation.surface: A patient who has been injured and fallen ill receives medical care and needs help walking.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on crutches relies on them for physical support when walking.

blocks.note: first meaning: excellent, dated slang
second meaning: to expand

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine balloon' reads as a nice balloon; 'balloon' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Swell is an old slang adjective for excellent and a verb for growing larger.

blocks.note: taken as written
to jar is to jolt

explanation.surface: A door flies open with a sudden jerk.
explanation.definitionFit: Ajar describes a door slightly open, so it can stand in for open as an adjective.

indicators.note: embracing someone wraps your arms around them, so one name goes around the other

blocks.note: a typical Spanish woman's name
another typical Spanish name

explanation.surface: One Spaniard hugs another, with a drug in the picture.
explanation.walkthrough: Any common Spanish first names will do; the right pair is found by fitting the letter count.
explanation.definitionFit: Marijuana is cannabis, a drug, and the word itself comes from Spanish.

indicators.note: an echo sends a sound back, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: B is a musical note
ever means always

explanation.surface: A musical description: a long note ringing on and on.
explanation.definitionFit: A breve is the longest note in common use, worth two semibreves.

clue.text: Sharp weapon, knife's back in box

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: to spar is to box in practice
last letter of knife

explanation.surface: A blade has been tucked into the back of a box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'box' looks like a container, but it is the verb, as in boxing.
explanation.definitionFit: A spear is a long pointed weapon for thrusting or throwing.

clue.text: Scattering is spread out and left

indicators.note: spread out suggests the letters are laid out in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to rearrange
L abbreviates left

explanation.surface: Something is spread far and wide and abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' feels like part of the definition, but it is fodder; 'out' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dispersal is the act of spreading things widely, a synonym of scattering as a noun.
